## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the three changes do what the description says for a non-zero level. One side effect is worth addressing: a keyboard deliberately turned off with the hotkeys can now come back on after a lock-then-sleep. Two smaller gaps that this PR does not introduce are noted below.

**Verified** in source and in sandboxed runs of the changed scripts:

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| Lock timer's suspend-gap branch calls `runWake()` | The call-graph analysis in the description holds. This branch was the only re-arm with no wake before it, and `runWake()` still re-arms while locked, so the 5 s run-up is kept. The repo's own hibernate hook (`default/systemd/system-sleep/keyboard-backlight`) sets the keyboard to 0 without saving; with an earlier level saved, head restores it where the merge-base recorded 0. |
| `restore` only writes at level 0 | A level changed with the hotkeys while locked, and a non-zero level changed before a screensaver dismissal (#10767), survive the wake. An empty or failed `get` falls back to the old unconditional restore, and with no saved file `brightnessctl -r` writes nothing. |
| Keyboard restored before the display in `omarchy-system-wake` | The keyboard level is back before the Hyprland IPC calls in `omarchy-brightness-display on` run. Without a keyboard backlight, the display wake still runs. |
| New test | 7/7 pass on head. With only the `OMARCHY_LEDS_PATH` seam applied to the merge-base, it fails at "restore leaves a level changed while blanked". On the untouched merge-base it stops earlier at device discovery, because the seam is missing. |

### A hotkey zero is relit after a lock-then-sleep

`up`, `down` and `cycle` set the level without updating the saved value, so `restore` cannot tell a hotkey zero from a blank. With the new suspend-gap wake, this now also affects sleeps that lock before the first blank (menu or `systemctl` suspend/hibernate, lid close):

```text
Earlier lock blank saved 40. User sets keyboard to 0 with the hotkeys, then a sleep path locks and suspends
before the 5 s blank. After resume, no input on the lock screen.

                          merge-base                 head
suspend-gap timer fires   re-arm only                runWake() -> restore sees 0, writes 40
blank 5 s later           saves 0, sets 0            saves 40, sets 0
unlock (restore)          keyboard 0, saved 0        keyboard 40, saved 40
```

The same gap already exists on the merge-base when the screensaver is dismissed after a hotkey zero, and when the lock screen gets input before the first blank. The test "restore keeps a deliberate zero off" starts with `off` capturing the zero, so it does not cover a hotkey zero with an older saved level.

**Impact:** a keyboard backlight turned off by hand comes back on after this kind of sleep, and again after unlock. This contradicts the description's statement that a deliberate zero is kept.

**Suggested change:** make the hotkey paths record the new level, for example `brightnessctl -sd "$device" get` after the `set` in `up`, `down` and `cycle`. A hotkey zero is then restored as zero on every path, and the level-0 guard still keeps changes made while locked. A test case with saved level 40, current level 0 and `restore` would cover it. Otherwise, narrow the deliberate-zero wording in the description.

**Residual gap, not introduced by this PR (dropped wake during an IPC stall):** `runWake()` drops a request while an earlier wake process is still running, but still re-arms the blank timer. If a wake spends more than 5 s in its display or clamshell step, the blank fires, and a later request is dropped, a second blank's `off` saves 0 over the good level. Once that sequence occurs, the result follows from the scripts and brightnessctl 0.5.1 on both the merge-base and head (checked with the real scripts and a stub that holds the display step; the QML decisions were modelled from source). How often the timing occurs was not measured. The reorder closes a related single-blank case on the merge-base. Since the description already cites IPC stalls, a `timeout` on the display and clamshell steps (as `omarchy-system-sleep-lock` does) or re-running a dropped wake when `wakeProcess` exits would close it.

**Residual gap, not introduced by this PR (first sleep of a login):** brightnessctl 0.5.1 keeps the saved level in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/brightnessctl`, so it is empty after a reboot or new login. If the first locked sleep brings the keyboard back at 0 before any blank has saved a level, `restore` has nothing to apply and the next blank saves 0. The hotkey change above would reduce this.

**Description note:** the suspend-gap branch only runs when the blank timer is still armed at suspend (the timer is one-shot). A lock that blanked more than 5 s before sleep has no pending timer. That case is already handled by the first input after resume, which restores the saved level on both branches. The fix therefore targets lock-then-sleep and input shortly before sleep, rather than every resume.
